data.name: Vishu
data.gender_notes: Vishu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Vishu is the name of the Hindu deity Vishnu in his form as the preserver and protector of the universe. The name Vishu is derived from the Sanskrit word vish, which means 'all-pervading'. Vishu is believed to bring prosperity and wealth to those who call upon him. The name Vishu carries the meaning “Lord of Wealth and Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Vishu usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of wealth and prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Vishu is a powerful name with deep spiritual significance. It represents the divine presence of Vishnu, the preserver and protector of the universe. Those named Vishu are believed to carry the blessings of Vishnu with them and to have a strong connection to the divine.
data.etymology: Vishu belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Wealth and Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vishu total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

It is considered an auspicious day to begin new projects and to decorate one's home with gold, silver, grains, fruits, and vegetables. During the festival, families gather to enjoy a delicious feast and seek the blessings of Vishnu.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Vishu holds tremendous spiritual significance for Hindus as it is associated with the divine deity Vishnu. Vishu is believed to be the embodiment of love, compassion, and preservation. He is the sustainer of the universe and the source of all good qualities. By calling upon the name Vishu, one invokes the divine presence and seeks his blessings for success, prosperity, and spiritual growth.
